rows.text: Clinic visit. 60-year-old male presents with three months of progressive fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and unusual cravings for ice. Denies melena or hematochezia but reports occasional dark stools. Exam: pale conjunctivae, resting tachycardia 104 bpm, systolic flow murmur at left sternal border. Started on oral ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times daily with vitamin C, stool occult blood testing ordered. Will recheck CBC and iron studies in six weeks. Advised on dietary iron sources and follow-up sooner if melena or lightheadedness develops.

rows.text: Urgent care. 86-year-old female brought in by her daughter with 5 days of productive cough with yellow sputum, low-grade fever to 100.2 F, sore throat, and mild hoarseness. No chest pain or dyspnea at rest. Exam: temperature 100.0 F, lungs with scattered rhonchi, no wheeze, no consolidatory findings, no egophony, O2 sat 96% on room air. Chest x-ray shows no infiltrate or consolidation — acute bronchitis, likely viral. Plan: supportive care with fluids, rest, guaifenesin, acetaminophen as needed for fever; no antibiotics indicated at this time. Return precautions reviewed for worsening dyspnea, high fever, or confusion. Follow-up with PCP if symptoms persist beyond 2-3 weeks.
